title: Example Rural Middle-Mile Resilience Opportunity
problem_statement: Critical community facilities in the eastern service area depend on a single constrained route, creating an observable continuity and capacity risk during outages.

evidence.claim: The county plan identifies inadequate broadband capacity in the eastern service area.
Three critical facilities appear to share one upstream transport route.
evidence.source: Public route maps and facility records
evidence.notes: Requires owner confirmation and field validation.

evidence.claim: A county department could sponsor a feasibility assessment.
The proposed corridor has usable public right-of-way.
evidence.notes: Rights-of-way review has not been completed.

evidence.claim: The project is eligible for a currently available funding program.
evidence.notes: Program eligibility and application authority remain unconfirmed.

problem_evidence.rationale: The adopted plan verifies the capacity problem; outage consequence needs additional operational evidence.

authority_clarity.rationale: A plausible public sponsor is visible, but buyer and final approval authority are not verified.

technical_fit.rationale: A redundant fiber route is plausible, subject to route ownership, field, and right-of-way validation.

funding_path.rationale: A funding path has not yet been connected to a verified eligible applicant and scope.

strategic_alignment.rationale: The assessment fits AnchorFiber asset, route, dependency, and opportunity-intelligence capabilities.

differentiated_advantage.rationale: Evidence-linked opportunity analysis and route-dependency modeling offer a bounded differentiator.

delivery_readiness.rationale: The intelligence assessment is deliverable, but engineering and deployment partners are not named.

risk_position.rationale: The largest uncertainties are explicit and can be tested, but funding and right-of-way remain material.

S.rationale: The geography, infrastructure condition, and affected facilities are bounded.

P.rationale: A capacity and route-resilience problem with operational consequences is supported.

A1.rationale: A sponsor is plausible, but procurement and approval authority require confirmation.

T.rationale: No fatal technical constraint is known; route and right-of-way validation remain open.

I.rationale: Funding availability and eligibility are unverified.

A2.rationale: A bounded AnchorFiber intelligence role is defined without assuming engineering authority.

known_limitations: This example uses fictional entities and is not a real market finding.
Route topology has not been confirmed by an asset owner.
No field survey, preliminary engineering, or funding eligibility review has been completed.

lifecycle.next_action: Confirm sponsor authority, route ownership, and funding eligibility through a bounded discovery review.
lifecycle.resource_ceiling: Eight analyst hours; no proposal or engineering spend authorized
revalidation_triggers: Sponsor authority is confirmed or denied
A relevant funding notice is issued
Evidence becomes more than 90 days old
